transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lara Kim (Arcadia ML Infra), Owen Reyes (Arcadia CTO), Samir Patel (Arcadia SRE)

Summary (auto): quick retune on throughput targets; reviewed last week's pilot numbers, proposed continuous-batching & concurrency cap changes, agreed on stress window and follow-ups.
Topics: throughput, continuous batching, queue depth, concurrency targets, tail latency, fallback model behavior, cost impact.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give folks a minute to pop in. um this is Maya from Redwood, with Ethan on the se side.
[00:28] Ethan: hey! hi all. quick agenda, review last week's numbers, show the retune suggestions we ran overnight, and lock down the 2 hour stress window and next steps.
[00:45] Lara: sounds good. we are short-staffed so thanks for keeping it tight.
[01:10] Owen: yeah, appreciate it. we mostly want to see p99 improvements without blowing up cost.
[01:30] Samir: and we care about backpressure — last week's spikes caused retries in our app tier.
[01:47] Maya: understood. Ethan, can you start with the bench highlights?
[01:54] Ethan: sure. quick context — the pilot runs we've been looking at were using continuous-batching enabled, but with a conservative queue depth cap of 40 and concurrency target 12 per GPU. Over the week we saw decent avg throughput but p99 tail at ~720ms which is above Arcadia's 500ms SLO.
[02:30] Ethan: we also saw frequent short bursts where queue depth would spike to 60-70 and then cause a cascade retry at the app layer. Some of that is workload variance — longer docs = KV cache misses — the k-v cache sometimes gets thrashed. transcription: "k v cache" in logs is spelled K V cache so needs mapping.
[03:05] Lara: quick question — when you say concurrency target 12, is that threads or sessions? we've been passing connection pool of 200 from the app earlier.
[03:20] Ethan: good point. it's per-inference-worker concurrency, so essentially simultaneous token generation streams on the GPU. App pool is higher; the front-end queueing sits in front of Redwood.
[03:38] Owen: and the long docs you mentioned, those are the 1.5k+ tokens few users have?
[03:46] Ethan: yep. percentile wise, 90th is ~900 tokens for the recommendation path.
[04:00] Maya: ok, so the tuning we propose is threefold: increase queue depth cap to 80 to buffer bursts, lower per-GPU concurrency to 9 to reduce head-of-line blocking, and enable prefix caching aggressively for the recommendation template path.
[04:25] Samir: lowering concurrency to 9 — won't that reduce throughput?
[04:33] Ethan: it can drop raw peak throughput but what we saw in tests is net increase in stable throughput because tail latency drops and retries go away. in our offline bench: tokens/sec steady state improved ~7% and p99 dropped to ~420ms with the new knobs.
[04:55] Lara: can you repeat the numbers? p50/p95/p99 after the change?
[05:02] Ethan: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms — prior was p99 ~720ms. idle GPU util rose slightly, but less noisy spikes.
[05:20] Owen: what about cost impact? our finance team wants to see delta on committed usage.
[05:27] Maya: cost note — with fewer retries and no added instances, unit cost per successful request dropped ~4.5% in bench. if we add burst capacity (reserve one extra slot for peak) that would be +~8% commit. We'll detail those numbers in the plan.
[05:48] Samir: the retries were the big hit for us — our logs show around 1.8% error/retry rate during the last 3 stress windows.
[06:00] Ethan: yep and many of those map to queue overflow at the ingress level. We also observed some model fallback events — when the primary large model hit mem pressure, service fell back to quantized variant and latency jumped further.
[06:22] Lara: interesting. is the fallback automatic or policy-driven?
[06:27] Ethan: it's policy-driven — we have a fallback to q4_0 variant when memory thresholds cross. The policy had been aggressive; we've relaxed it in the proposed profile so we only fallback after p95 memory cross threshold for 30s.
[06:47] Owen: so we get fewer fallback flips which should reduce output variance. good.
[07:00] Maya: also we recommend prefix-level caching for the top 12 recommendation prompts — that cuts token generation on the root prefix by about 35% in our microbench.
[07:18] Lara: will that change correctness? some results rely on recency tokens.
[07:25] Ethan: prefix caching is conditional — only when context doesn't include personalization tokens. we'll share the rule set (link to cache rules doc).
[07:40] Samir: can you share the bench sheet? the team wants raw Prometheus and the xlsx.
[07:46] Maya: yes, I'll attach the Redwood bench sheet and the Prometheus dump. link: https://redwood.corp/pilot/arcadia/bench-20260305 (internal link).
[08:05] Owen: perfect.
[08:10] Ethan: next bit — concurrency floor vs cap. We propose a floor of 6 and cap 12 per GPU, with dynamic scaling: when average queue depth > 55 for 2min we increment concurrency by 1 up to cap; when avg qdepth < 20 for 3min we decrement. This keeps latency stable while reacting to sustained load.
[08:40] Lara: that dynamic feels safer. does that require a config change on your control plane?
[08:46] Ethan: minimal — it's a rollout flag in the route config. We'll push to the pilot namespace first.
[08:55] Samir: and what's the expected behavior if we hit an outage in the region? will requests failover to another region with different model variants?
[09:05] Maya: right now we have cross-region fallback but it falls back to a smaller model variant to preserve latency. There is a cost and possibly slight quality delta; we'll document tradeoffs.
[09:20] Owen: anything about batching window? are you still using 8ms max batching window?
[09:28] Ethan: yes we had 8ms, we tested increasing to 12ms in low-latency paths and it netted ~3% improvement in batch efficiency without noticeable p99 regressions after lowering concurrency. But we prefer conservative 10ms as a compromise.
[09:48] Lara: so the combined proposal: qdepth cap 80, concurrency target 9 with floor 6 and cap 12 dynamic ramps, batching window 10ms, relaxed fallback policy, prefix caching for top templates.
[10:05] Ethan: exactly. we ran a simulated 4 hour run overnight on pilot cluster with a replay of last week's traffic and these knobs — results are in the sheet.
[10:18] Maya: quick note on observability — we've added trace hooks so you can map retries to queue events and GPU mem pressure. that should help root cause.
[10:30] Samir: great. i also want to call out that our infra has a hard limit on ephemeral storage; will prefix caching increase local disk usage?
[10:40] Ethan: small increase, but cache lives in memory primarily; disk usage for local index is negligible.
[10:52] Owen: okay let's talk about the stress window. we propose next Wednesday 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC for a 2h run — Arcadia will route real traffic (canary) and we'll monitor.
[11:05] Lara: that slot works for us, Samir?
[11:09] Samir: yeah, confirmed.
[11:12] Maya: good. action items: i'll send the updated plan and commit pricing; Ethan will deploy the config to pilot; Arcadia will run the window and upload logs.
[11:24] Owen: one more question on SLOs — if p99 still misses, are there tradeoffs we can accept temporarily?
[11:31] Maya: options: increase concurrency cap, add a burst instance, or allow controlled fallback to smaller model during peak windows — each has cost/quality tradeoffs. we'll lay them out in the plan.
[11:45] Lara: and what about alerting — we need alert thresholds for queue depth and fallback flips.
[11:50] Ethan: we'll seed alerts: qdepth > 70 for 1m and fallback flips > 3 in 5m; we can tune.
[11:58] Samir: perfect.
[12:05] Maya: any other blockers?
[12:09] Owen: nothing from engineering side. finance will want the cost delta but that's off this call.
[12:18] Maya: ok wrap up — recap next steps and who owns what.
[12:22] (short crosstalk)
[12:30] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with links, bench sheet, and exact config. meeting ends.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Bench summary: retune produced p99 420ms, tokens/sec +7% steady state, retries reduced from 1.8% to 0.3% in replay.
- Risks: prefix caching may require extra rules for personalization; fallback policy relaxation could increase memory pressure if not monitored.
- Documents shared: bench sheet (link above), cache rules doc (will attach), rollout config snippet (will attach).
